content.Indication: Consider when baseline clinical assessment suggests cardiac inflammation or storage disease not diagnosed by other means.
content.Therapeutic options: Outlined; see references. Separate recommendations for patients with LVOTO and those symptomatic without LVOTO.
content.With LVOTO: Avoid hypovolaemia, arterial/venous dilators and digoxin; use non-vasodilating beta-blockers or verapamil if beta-blockers not tolerated; cautious use of low-dose diuretics; consider invasive septal reduction (alcohol ablation or myomectomy) in experienced centres for resting or provoked LVOT gradient ≥50 mmHg and/or persistent symptoms (NYHA III/IV, syncope) despite OMT; novel drugs/devices may be considered when available.
content.Symptomatic without LVOTO: Cautious low-dose diuretics avoiding hypovolaemia; verapamil/diltiazem if LVEF >50% and beta-blockers not tolerated/ineffective.
content.Indication to ICD: Based on sudden cardiac death risk models; consider ICD if family history of sudden cardiac death in first-degree relatives under 40 or sudden cardiac death in first-degree relative with confirmed HCM at any age, NSVT, unexplained syncope, or other risk markers per guidelines.
content.Fabry disease: Enzyme replacement therapy for alpha-galactosidase A deficiency mentioned.
content.Abbreviations (selected visible): Includes BAG3 = Bcl2-associated athanogene 3; LMNA = lamin A/C; ECG, HCM, ICD, LGE, LVEF, LVOTO and others.
